n-12-n12b1-q001.boardCall: Buttock claudication + erectile dysfunction + diminished pedal pulses -> aortoiliac occlusion (Leriche syndrome)
n-12-n12b1-q001.hinge: Exertional buttock pain relieved by rest and absent pulses indicate aortoiliac occlusion.
n-12-n12b1-q001.trap: Low back pain radiating to the buttocks mimics spinal stenosis or lumbar disc disease.

A.fit: Here: buttock claudication relieved by rest, erectile dysfunction, decreased pulses

B.fit: Not here: 1-year progressive symptoms, no acute tearing pain
B.tempting: aortic vascular pathology causing lower extremity symptoms

C.clue: Sciatica, positive straight-leg raise
C.fit: Not here: negative straight-leg raise, relief within 1 minute

D.fit: Not here: afebrile, normal ESR, exertion-dependent pain relieved by rest

nodes.text: Exertional buttock, hip, or thigh claudication: assess femoral and pedal pulses
**Pulses intact with postural relief:** evaluate for lumbar spinal stenosis
Measure ankle-brachial index (ABI)
**ABI <= 0.90:** obtain duplex ultrasound or CT angiography
Initiate smoking cessation + high-intensity statin + aspirin
Prescribe supervised exercise therapy
**Disabling lifestyle claudication or rest ischemia:** surgical bypass or endovascular revascularization

n-12-n12b1-q002.boardCall: Postmenopausal woman with tobacco history -> cardiovascular disease is greatest mortality risk
n-12-n12b1-q002.hinge: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death in postmenopausal women.
n-12-n12b1-q002.trap: Long smoking history makes lung cancer tempting, but cardiovascular mortality is higher.

A.fit: Not here: normal mammogram, CVD causes far more deaths
A.tempting: common malignancy in postmenopausal women

B.clue: Leading cause of death in women
B.fit: Here: postmenopausal status, 40 pack-years, obesity, high waist-to-hip ratio

C.clue: HPV infection, postcoital bleeding
C.fit: Not here: normal Pap smear, low absolute mortality rate
C.tempting: female malignancy requiring routine screening

D.clue: Bone mineral density decline
D.fit: Not here: no history of fractures, CVD mortality predominates

algorithm.title: Cardiovascular risk reduction in postmenopausal women

nodes.text: Loss of estrogen protection increases cardiovascular disease risk: primary cause of mortality
Calculate 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk score
Counsel on smoking cessation + Mediterranean diet + regular exercise
**Elevated cardiovascular risk or LDL-C >= 190:** start statin therapy
**Blood pressure >= 130/80 mm Hg:** initiate antihypertensive medication
Screen annually with blood pressure + fasting lipid profile

n-12-n12b1-q003.boardCall: Acute dyspnea + hyperresonance + absent breath sounds -> tube thoracostomy
n-12-n12b1-q003.hinge: Large symptomatic pneumothorax with hypoxia requires immediate tube thoracostomy.
n-12-n12b1-q003.trap: Asthma history tempts bronchodilators, but asymmetric breath sounds and hyperresonance indicate pneumothorax.

A.clue: Refractory hypoxia, impending arrest
A.fit: Not here: alert, breathing spontaneously, no impending airway failure

B.fit: Not here: unilateral absent breath sounds, no diffuse wheezing
B.tempting: known history of mild asthma

C.fit: Not here: oxygen saturation 92%, significant dyspnea

D.fit: Not here: closed spontaneous pneumothorax, hemodynamically stable

nodes.text: Sudden pleuritic chest pain + unilateral diminished breath sounds: assess stability
**Tension pneumothorax (hypotension, tracheal shift):** emergent needle thoracostomy
Obtain upright chest radiograph
**Small pneumothorax (< 2 cm) + asymptomatic:** supplemental oxygen + observation
**Large pneumothorax (>= 2 cm) or symptomatic hypoxia:** insert tube thoracostomy
Connect thoracostomy tube to water-seal drainage and repeat radiograph
**Persistent air leak > 48 hours:** perform video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery

n-12-n12b1-q004.boardCall: Isolated severe thrombocytopenia + menorrhagia in adolescent -> immune thrombocytopenic purpura
n-12-n12b1-q004.hinge: Isolated severe thrombocytopenia with normal hemoglobin and leukocyte count indicates ITP.
n-12-n12b1-q004.trap: Fever and thrombocytopenia tempt TTP, but hemolysis, schistocytes, and neurologic/renal findings are absent.

A.clue: Everted columnar cervical epithelium
A.fit: Not here: platelet count 15,000/mm³, not a local anatomical cause
A.tempting: heavy vaginal bleeding in adolescent

B.clue: Focal intrauterine endometrial outgrowth
B.fit: Not here: severe systemic thrombocytopenia, normal pelvic anatomy
B.tempting: prolonged vaginal bleeding

C.clue: Antiplatelet antibodies, isolated low platelets
C.fit: Here: platelets 15,000/mm³, heavy menses, otherwise normal cell lines

D.clue: Uterine smooth muscle benign neoplasm
D.fit: Not here: severe thrombocytopenia 15,000/mm³, normal pelvic exam

E.clue: Pentad with microangiopathic hemolysis

nodes.text: Isolated thrombocytopenia + mucosal bleeding: review peripheral blood smear
**Schistocytes present:** evaluate for thrombotic microangiopathy or DIC
Rule out secondary causes (HIV, hepatitis C virus, systemic lupus erythematosus)
**Platelets < 30,000/mm³ or active bleeding:** administer oral prednisone or IVIG
**Life-threatening hemorrhage:** platelet transfusion + IVIG + high-dose methylprednisolone
Avoid NSAIDs, antiplatelet agents, and contact sports
**Relapsed or chronic ITP:** initiate thrombopoietin receptor agonists or rituximab

n-12-n12b1-q005.hinge: Vascular encasement of superior mesenteric vessels precludes curative resection, determining poor prognosis.
n-12-n12b1-q005.trap: High conjugated bilirubin reflects ductal occlusion, but vascular encasement dictates unresectability.

A.clue: Common bile duct compression marker
A.fit: Not here: reflects biliary duct compression, does not define surgical resectability
A.tempting: direct bilirubin of 5.2 mg/dL

B.clue: Chronologic age baseline
B.fit: Not here: age 49 is young, vascular invasion drives mortality
B.tempting: general surgical candidate risk factor

C.clue: Biological sex epidemiology
C.fit: Not here: sex assigned at birth does not dictate cancer resectability
C.tempting: male sex slight predominance

D.clue: Superior mesenteric vascular invasion
D.fit: Here: partially encasing superior mesenteric artery, precluding curative resection

E.clue: Early jaundice presentation
E.fit: Not here: head lesions present earlier than tail, better prognosis
E.tempting: pancreatic head mass location

nodes.text: Painless jaundice + weight loss: obtain multiphase pancreatic-protocol abdominal CT
Tumor encasement of superior mesenteric vessels predicts unresectability and poor prognosis
Perform endoscopic ultrasound with fine-needle biopsy for tissue diagnosis
**Resectable disease (no arterial encasement):** surgical pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple)
**Locally advanced or unresectable:** initiate gemcitabine-based systemic chemotherapy
Place biliary stent for pruritus or severe hyperbilirubinemia

nontender mass is palpated in the right upper quadrant

partially encasing the superior mesenteric artery

n-12-n12b1-q006.hinge: Elevated jugular venous distension, bibasilar pulmonary crackles, and an S3 gallop confirm heart failure.
n-12-n12b1-q006.trap: Arteriolar narrowing and high blood pressure tempt renal artery stenosis, but acute pulmonary edema is CHF.

A.clue: Infiltrative cardiomyopathy with low voltage
A.fit: Not here: no low ECG voltage, hypertension drives left ventricular dysfunction
A.tempting: restrictive signs with diastolic dysfunction

B.clue: Chronic intimal flap, tearing back pain
B.fit: Not here: no history of tearing chest pain, clear heart failure
B.tempting: hypertensive vascular complication

C.clue: Elevated filling pressures, crackles, S3
C.fit: Here: S3, S4, bibasilar crackles, distended jugular veins, dyspnea

D.clue: Pericardial thickening, Kussmaul sign
D.fit: Not here: prominent lung crackles, no pericardial knock or calcification
D.tempting: jugular venous distension and dyspnea

nodes.text: Acute dyspnea + bibasilar crackles + elevated JVD: obtain ECG + BNP + chest x-ray
Perform transthoracic echocardiography to assess left ventricular function
Administer IV loop diuretics to relieve pulmonary congestion
**Persistent congestion + elevated blood pressure:** add IV nitroglycerin
**Cardiogenic shock (hypotension, organ hypoperfusion):** initiate inotropic support
Initiate guideline-directed medical therapy with beta blockers and ACE inhibitors

arteriolar narrowing but no papilledema

n-12-n12b1-q007.hinge: Physical features of extreme nonviability (< 22-23 weeks) and failure to respond indicate discontinuing resuscitation.
n-12-n12b1-q007.trap: Extreme bradycardia tempts epinephrine or intubation, but nonviable gestational age precludes survival.

A.clue: Continued CPR in viable arrest
A.fit: Not here: nonviable anatomical development, continued CPR is nonbeneficial
A.tempting: pulse remains present though severely bradycardic

B.clue: Respiratory distress in viable preterm
B.fit: Not here: nonviable gestational age with primitive nonfunctioning lungs
B.tempting: extreme prematurity causes surfactant deficiency

C.clue: Invasive airway in viable arrest
C.fit: Not here: immature brainstem and lungs preclude survival below viability
C.tempting: unresponsive to bag-valve-mask ventilation

D.clue: Vascular access for neonatal arrest
D.fit: Not here: nonviable newborn (< 22 weeks), invasive resuscitation contraindicated

E.clue: Recognition of extreme nonviability
E.fit: Here: 500 g, fused eyelids, absent spontaneous respirations despite CPR

algorithm.title: Delivery room management of periviable birth

nodes.text: Extremely preterm delivery: rapidly assess gestational age and viability signs
**Viable infant (>= 24 weeks):** initiate full neonatal resuscitation protocol
Assess signs of nonviability (< 22-23 weeks): birth weight < 500 grams + fused eyelids
Discontinue resuscitative efforts when nonviability is confirmed
Provide compassionate comfort care and wrap infant warmly
Support grieving family and discuss bereavement resources

pulse of 30/min

n-12-n12b1-q008.boardCall: Intubated burn patient + NG tube + purulent nasal drainage -> CT scan of the sinuses
n-12-n12b1-q008.hinge: Fever and purulent nasal discharge around a nasogastric tube point to nosocomial sinusitis.
n-12-n12b1-q008.trap: Cloudy drainage near NG tube might tempt abdominal imaging, but nasal source indicates sinusitis.

A.clue: Pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea, tachycardia
A.fit: Not here: lungs clear, purulent nasal discharge points to sinus infection
A.tempting: hospitalized burn patient at risk for DVT

B.clue: Abdominal tenderness, peritoneal signs
B.fit: Not here: abdomen soft and nontender, clear sinus discharge
B.tempting: fever with nasogastric tube drainage

C.clue: Purulent nasal discharge with nasogastric tube
C.fit: Here: nasogastric tube, purulent nasal drainage, fever 38.9°C, leukocytosis

D.clue: Perianal pain, fluctuance, induration
D.fit: Not here: normal rectal examination, purulent nasal discharge present

nodes.text: Fever in intubated patient with nasogastric tube: examine for nasal discharge
Obtain CT scan of the paranasal sinuses
**Sinus opacification or air-fluid levels:** remove nasogastric tube
Perform endoscopic sinus aspiration for bacterial culture
Initiate empiric IV antibiotics covering Pseudomonas and Gram-negative organisms
**Refractory to antimicrobial therapy:** perform surgical endoscopic sinus drainage

n-12-n12b1-q009.boardCall: Recurrent pneumonia + severe chickenpox + thrush + low CD4 -> combined immunodeficiency
n-12-n12b1-q009.hinge: Combined cellular and humoral defect causing opportunistic fungal, viral, and bacterial infections.
n-12-n12b1-q009.trap: Recurrent pneumonia tempts X-linked agammaglobulinemia, but severe chickenpox and oral thrush require T-cell defect.

A.clue: T- and B-cell deficiency, opportunistic infections
A.fit: Here: recurrent pneumonia, chickenpox, oral thrush, CD4 count 225/mm³

B.clue: Bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, sweat chloride
B.fit: Not here: severe viral chickenpox and low CD4, not CFTR defect
B.tempting: failure to thrive and recurrent pneumonia

C.clue: Impaired antibody production, recurrent sinopulmonary infections
C.fit: Not here: severe viral and fungal infections show T-cell involvement
C.tempting: recurrent bacterial pneumonia in young child

D.clue: Hypocalcemia, cardiac defects, thymic aplasia
D.fit: Not here: no conotruncal heart defect or dysmorphic facial features
D.tempting: T-cell deficiency and low CD4 count

E.clue: BTK mutation, absent circulating B cells
E.fit: Not here: thrush and severe varicella indicate T-cell cellular defect
E.tempting: recurrent pneumonia after amoxicillin

nodes.text: Recurrent severe infections (fungal, viral, bacterial) + failure to thrive: obtain lymphocyte counts
Evaluate T-cell deficiency: flow cytometry for CD3, CD4, CD8, CD19
**Marked T lymphopenia (CD4 < 500):** test lymphocyte mitogen proliferation
Start antimicrobial prophylaxis with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole + fluconazole + IVIG
Avoid all live vaccines and administer irradiated CMV-negative blood products
**Confirmed combined immunodeficiency:** perform allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation

oral thrush

n-12-n12b1-q010.hinge: Hypoventilation from opioid toxicity causes hypercapnia, which is confirmed by arterial blood gas.
n-12-n12b1-q010.trap: Postoperative acute unresponsiveness tempts head CT for stroke, but bradypnea and pinpoint pupils indicate opioid toxicity.

A.clue: Rapid assessment of pH and PaCO2
A.fit: Here: respirations 6/min, pupils 3 mm, postoperative hydromorphone exposure

B.clue: Leukocytosis or acute severe anemia
B.fit: Not here: surgical site clean, no acute bleeding, bradypnea predominates
B.tempting: postoperative anemia or surgical site hemorrhage

C.clue: Electrolyte derangements or hyperosmolarity
C.fit: Not here: acute severe hypoventilation not explained by electrolyte shifts
C.tempting: metabolic encephalopathy causing decreased responsiveness

D.clue: Acute intracranial hemorrhage or stroke
D.fit: Not here: no focal neurologic deficit, respirations 6/min with miosis
D.tempting: acute loss of consciousness postoperatively

E.fit: Not here: severe bradypnea 6/min, whereas PE presents with tachypnea
E.tempting: postoperative orthopedic patient at risk for PE

nodes.text: Unresponsiveness + respirations <= 8/min + miosis: assess airway and breathing
Obtain arterial blood gas analysis to assess hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis
Provide bag-valve-mask assisted ventilation with supplemental oxygen
Administer IV naloxone titrated to reverse respiratory depression
**Inadequate response to initial naloxone:** repeat naloxone bolus or continuous infusion
**Persistent hypoxemia or airway compromise:** endotracheal intubation
Discontinue all opioid and sedating medications and monitor in stepdown unit

n-12-q091.hinge: Persistent depressed mood and flat affect beyond postpartum blues duration warrants SSRI therapy.
n-12-q091.trap: Postpartum amenorrhea and weight gain tempt hormonal therapy, but primary pathology is major depression.

A.fit: Not here: normal neurologic examination and no headaches or focal deficits
A.tempting: amenorrhea and mood changes can raise pituitary adenoma concerns

B.clue: Dopamine antagonist indicated for postpartum psychosis
B.fit: Not here: patient has no psychotic symptoms, delusions, or hallucinations
B.tempting: mood disturbance after childbirth can progress to psychosis

C.fit: Not here: postpartum anovulation is expected 5 weeks post-weaning
C.tempting: evaluates secondary amenorrhea and anovulatory cycles

D.clue: Hormone replacement for hypoestrogenism in ovarian failure

E.clue: First-line pharmacotherapy for postpartum depression
E.fit: Here: persistent postpartum depression, crying, flat affect, and loss of interest

nodes.text: Distinguish postpartum blues (< 2 weeks, mild tearfulness) from postpartum depression (> 2 weeks)
Screen for postpartum psychosis: delusions, hallucinations, confusion, infanticidal ideation
**Psychosis or infanticidal thoughts:** emergency psychiatric admission + antipsychotic therapy
Moderate to severe postpartum depression: initiate SSRI therapy (sertraline preferred)
**Severe treatment-resistant depression:** brexanolone IV infusion or ECT
Combine pharmacotherapy with cognitive behavioral therapy or interpersonal psychotherapy
Ensure safety of infant and arrange frequent follow-up monitoring

discontinuation of breast-feeding 5 weeks ago
flat affect and is slow to respond

n-12-q092.boardCall: Preeclampsia with severe features in labor -> Abruptio placentae
n-12-q092.hinge: Uteroplacental vascular disease and hypertension in preeclampsia predispose to placental abruption.
n-12-q092.trap: Severe hypertension can cause maternal stroke or death, but placental abruption is the most common obstetric complication.

A.clue: Premature placental detachment from decidual basalis hemorrhage
A.fit: Here: severe preeclampsia with hypertension, arteriolar spasm, and proteinuria

B.clue: Catastrophic entry of fetal tissue into circulation
B.fit: Not here: rare acute cardiorespiratory collapse and DIC without preeclampsia link
B.tempting: peripartum emergency causing sudden collapse and coagulopathy

C.clue: Failure of cervical dilation despite contractions
C.fit: Not here: cervix is already 3 cm and 100% effaced with active contractions
C.tempting: maternal hypertension can disrupt uterine contractile coordination

D.clue: Mortality endpoint averted by contemporary obstetric care
D.fit: Not here: rare outcome prevented with prompt magnesium and blood pressure control
D.tempting: severe preeclampsia carries potential risk of maternal mortality

E.clue: Uterine wall disruption occurring with prior scar
E.fit: Not here: occurs almost exclusively in patients with prior uterine scar or overdistension
E.tempting: intense uterine contractions in multigravida labor

nodes.text: Recognize preeclampsia with severe features: BP > 160/110, renal dysfunction, or visual symptoms
Most common obstetric complication is abruptio placentae due to uteroplacental vasculopathy
Administer IV magnesium sulfate to prevent eclamptic seizures
Administer IV labetalol or hydralazine for severe hypertension
Proceed with prompt delivery at > 37 weeks (or > 34 weeks with severe features)
**Evidence of placental abruption:** urgent cesarean delivery
Continue postpartum magnesium sulfate for 24 hours

n-12-q093.hinge: Autosomal dominant CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion in HTT gene confirms Huntington chorea.
n-12-q093.trap: Wilson disease can cause young-onset movement disorders, but slow saccades and classic chorea point to Huntington.

A.clue: Electrophysiologic recording detecting epileptiform discharges
A.fit: Not here: indicates seizures or Creutzfeldt-Jakob, not degenerative chorea
A.tempting: evaluates unexplained behavioral changes and involuntary twitches

B.clue: Delayed observation inappropriate for progressive disorder
B.fit: Not here: progressive 2-year neurocognitive decline requires definitive diagnostic evaluation
B.tempting: allows monitoring of subtle movement abnormalities over time

C.clue: CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion analysis on HTT
C.fit: Here: adult personality change, slow saccadic movements, and involuntary chorea

D.clue: CSF examination evaluating inflammatory central disorders
D.fit: Not here: indolent progressive subcortical dementia lacks infectious CSF pleocytosis
D.tempting: evaluates subacute encephalopathy or autoimmune encephalitis

E.clue: Copper transport screening detecting hepatolenticular degeneration
E.fit: Not here: Wilson disease presents with Kayser-Fleischer rings, tremor, and hepatic disease
E.tempting: young adult presenting with psychiatric symptoms and movement disorder

F.clue: Symptom rating scale without etiologic confirmation
F.fit: Not here: psychiatric assessment treats symptoms but misses primary Huntington genetic etiology

nodes.text: Recognize triad: motor (chorea, slow saccades), cognitive decline, psychiatric/personality changes
Diagnostic confirmation: targeted genetic testing for HTT gene CAG trinucleotide expansion
**> 39 CAG repeats:** fully penetrant Huntington disease
**36-39 CAG repeats:** reduced penetrance Huntington disease
Brain MRI: bilateral caudate nucleus and putamen atrophy with ventricular enlargement
Manage chorea: VMAT2 inhibitors (tetrabenazine, deutetrabenazine) or atypical antipsychotics
Provide pre-test genetic counseling for at-risk family members

algorithm.title: Imperforate hymen and vaginal outflow tract obstruction

nodes.text: Recognize clinical presentation: adolescent with primary amenorrhea + cyclical pelvic pain
Inspect external genitalia: tense, bluish, translucent bulging membrane at introitus
Transabdominal pelvic ultrasound: evaluate hematocolpos, hematometra, and pelvic anatomy
**Massive hematometra or hydronephrosis:** prioritize urgent surgical drainage
Definitive management: cruciate hymenotomy with excision of excess hymenal tissue
Dilation and catheter placement to prevent scar re-closure
Postoperative inspection: confirm normal internal vaginal and cervical anatomy

nodes.text: Determine age of pubertal onset (breast thelarche or pubic adrenarche)
**Onset at age 8 or older:** normal female puberty; provide reassurance and anticipatory guidance
**Onset before age 8 (precocious puberty):** order bone age radiograph of left hand/wrist
**Advanced bone age:** check baseline serum LH and FSH levels
**Normal bone age:** diagnose isolated premature thelarche or adrenarche; monitor closely
**Elevated basal or GnRH-stimulated LH:** central precocious puberty; order brain MRI
**Suppressed LH:** peripheral precocious puberty; obtain pelvic ultrasound and adrenal imaging

triggers.text: A 9-year-old girl is brought to the physician

algorithm.title: Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) evaluation and management

nodes.text: Recognize marked leukocytosis with full myeloid spectrum (myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands, neutrophils)
Differentiate CML (low LAP score, basophilia) from leukemoid reaction (high LAP score)
Diagnostic confirmation: cytogenetics or RT-PCR for Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) BCR-ABL1
Bone marrow biopsy: assess blast percentage to stage disease (chronic vs accelerated vs blast phase)
**Chronic phase (< 10% blasts):** initiate tyrosine kinase inhibitor (imatinib, dasatinib, or nilotinib)
**Accelerated or blast phase (> 20% blasts):** high-intensity chemo + allogeneic stem cell transplant
Monitor molecular response with quantitative BCR-ABL1 transcripts every 3 months

algorithm.title: Pediatric febrile urinary tract infection evaluation

nodes.text: Obtain renal and bladder ultrasound (RBUS) for first febrile UTI in children

**Abnormal ultrasound (hydronephrosis, scarring, or obstruction):** order voiding cystourethrography (VCUG)

Grade vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) from grade I to grade V based on VCUG findings
**High-grade reflux (grades III-V):** daily antibiotic prophylaxis or ureteral reimplantation
Order DMSA renal scintigraphy if needed to evaluate permanent renal cortical scarring

algorithm.title: Neonatal jaundice in first 24 hours: ABO incompatibility

nodes.text: Recognize pathologic jaundice: onset within first 24 hours of life
Differential: ABO incompatibility, Rh isoimmunization, G6PD deficiency, spherocytosis, sepsis

Initiate intensive phototherapy based on hour-specific bilirubin nomogram

algorithm.title: Management of post-extubation hypoxemia in obesity

nodes.text: Recognize post-extubation positional desaturation: sat > 95% sitting, 86% supine

**Development of hypercapnic respiratory failure:** trial noninvasive positive pressure ventilation (BiPAP)
Reintubate only if acute respiratory distress, severe acidosis, or hemodynamic collapse ensues

algorithm.title: Human factors engineering and patient safety design

nodes.text: Hierarchy of safety interventions: architectural/system designs are most effective, human memory least
Forcing function: hard physical or digital constraint making wrong actions impossible
**Examples:** computerized order entry hard stops, keyed gas connectors, blood lock boxes
Constraint: design limitation that restricts user actions to safe pathways
Affordance: visual or physical cue indicating how an object is naturally operated
Mapping: intuitive spatial relationship between controls and their actual movements
Standardization: reducing unnecessary variation to eliminate cognitive error

algorithm.title: Attributable risk calculation in cohort studies

nodes.text: Prospective cohort study: identify incidence of disease in exposed and unexposed groups
Calculate risk in exposed group: Ie = a / (a + b)
Calculate baseline risk in unexposed group: Iu = c / (c + d)
Calculate attributable risk: AR = Ie - Iu
**Interpret AR:** excess disease incidence directly attributable to the exposure
**Calculate attributable risk percent:** ARP = (Ie - Iu) / Ie

**Sinusoidal fetal heart pattern:** emergent delivery or intrauterine transfusion for severe fetal anemia
Evaluate fetal anemia using middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity Doppler
**MCA Doppler indicates severe anemia:** perform cordocentesis and intrauterine transfusion
**Near term or mature gestation:** proceed with urgent delivery
Administer anti-D immune globulin routinely to un-sensitized Rh-negative mothers

triggers.text: blood group is A, Rh-negative; a serum anti-D antibody titer is positive
During the next 30 minutes, fetal heart monitoring shows regular, sinusoidal wave forms
received no prenatal care
the vertex is at 0 station

n-12-n12b1-q037.boardCall: Chronic daytime sleepiness despite adequate sleep in young adult -> multiple sleep latency tests
n-12-n12b1-q037.hinge: Excessive daytime sleepiness without airway obstruction or sleep deprivation is evaluated with multiple sleep latency testing for narcolepsy.
n-12-n12b1-q037.trap: Overnight pulse oximetry screens for obstructive sleep apnea, but this young normal-weight woman lacks snoring or apneas.

A.clue: Standardized psychological personality inventory
A.fit: Not here: organic sleep disorder workup should precede psychiatric evaluation
A.tempting: evaluates somatization or factitious disorder

B.clue: Nocturnal oxygen saturation monitoring for sleep apnea
B.fit: Not here: normal BMI 21 kg/m², neat bedsheets, no snoring; polysomnography preferred
B.tempting: evaluates nocturnal hypoxemia and sleep apnea

C.clue: Spirometry and lung volume measurements
C.fit: Not here: cardiopulmonary system normal, central sleep disorder suspected
C.tempting: investigates respiratory causes of fatigue

D.clue: Brain magnetic resonance imaging for CNS lesions
D.fit: Not here: normal neurologic exam, objective electrophysiologic sleep study needed first
D.tempting: rules out intracranial mass causing somnolence

E.clue: Electrophysiologic testing of sleep latency and REM
E.fit: Here: daytime somnolence despite 8 hours sleep, normal weight, no snoring

nodes.text: Chronic excessive daytime sleepiness despite adequate sleep duration: exclude sleep apnea
Perform overnight polysomnography followed by next-day multiple sleep latency test
**Mean sleep latency <= 8 minutes + >= 2 sleep-onset REM periods:** confirm narcolepsy
Prescribe daytime wake-promoting agents: modafinil, armodafinil, or solriamfetol
**Cataplexy present:** prescribe sodium oxybate, venlafaxine, or fluoxetine
Counsel on planned daytime naps and strict sleep hygiene

triggers.text: 3-year history of falling asleep during her classes
goes to bed between midnight and 1 AM and gets up at 8 AM
tried sleeping for longer durations, even up to 8½ hours
BMI is 21 kg/m²
no one has ever told her that she snores

n-12-n12b1-q038.boardCall: Goiter + high TSH + bradycardia + negative anti-TPO on lithium -> medication adverse effect
n-12-n12b1-q038.hinge: Lithium impairs thyroid hormone synthesis and release, leading to goitrous primary hypothyroidism.
n-12-n12b1-q038.trap: Negative anti-TPO antibodies rule out Hashimoto thyroiditis; elevated TSH rules out pituitary dysfunction.

A.clue: Hashimoto thyroiditis with anti-TPO antibodies
A.fit: Not here: antithyroid peroxidase antibody testing is negative
A.tempting: common cause of primary hypothyroidism with goiter

B.clue: Sarcoidosis or histiocytosis infiltrating thyroid
B.fit: Not here: no systemic granulomatous manifestations, clear lithium drug exposure
B.tempting: causes nontender diffuse goiter

C.clue: Dietary lack of micronutrient in endemic areas
C.fit: Not here: rare in industrialized nations with iodized table salt access
C.tempting: classic cause of endemic goiter

D.clue: Drug-induced inhibition of thyroid hormone synthesis
D.fit: Here: long-term lithium therapy, firm goiter, TSH 25 µU/mL, negative anti-TPO

E.clue: Secondary hypothyroidism from anterior pituitary failure
E.fit: Not here: TSH is markedly elevated (25 µU/mL), which excludes pituitary failure
E.tempting: causes fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain

nodes.text: Patient on long-term lithium with fatigue, weight gain, or goiter: check serum TSH
Lithium inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis and secretion: medication-induced hypothyroidism
**Elevated TSH + normal or low free T4:** confirm primary hypothyroidism
Initiate oral levothyroxine hormone replacement therapy
Continue lithium therapy if psychiatric stability is maintained
**Monitoring:** repeat serum TSH every 6 to 12 months

triggers.text: medications are metformin, lisinopril, lithium, and pravastatin
pulse is 50/min
firm, nontender, symmetrically enlarged thyroid gland
serum thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration is 25 µU/mL
Antithyroid peroxidase antibody testing is negative

n-12-n12b1-q039.boardCall: Cephalexin exposure + acute urticaria + bilateral wheezing + hypotension -> anaphylactic reaction
n-12-n12b1-q039.hinge: Acute multisystem IgE-mediated allergic reaction with bronchospasm, generalized urticaria, and hypotension is anaphylaxis.
n-12-n12b1-q039.trap: Toxic shock causes hypotension and rash, but acute wheezing and urticaria immediately following cephalexin indicate anaphylaxis.

A.clue: IgE-mediated mast cell activation with bronchospasm
A.fit: Here: cephalexin exposure, acute urticaria, diffuse wheezes, blood pressure 90/60

B.clue: Rickettsial tick-borne vasculitis with petechial rash
B.fit: Not here: no tick bite, hyperacute bronchospasm and urticaria occur after antibiotic
B.tempting: presents with fever, rash on extremities, and hypotension

C.clue: Staphylococcal exfoliative toxin causing epidermal cleavage
C.fit: Not here: no flaccid bullae, desquamation, or Nikolsky sign; bronchospasm present
C.tempting: complication of cutaneous staphylococcal infection

D.clue: Superantigen toxin shock with erythroderma and desquamation
D.fit: Not here: afebrile, acute wheezing and pruritic urticaria point to anaphylaxis
D.tempting: causes acute hypotension and skin eruption

E.clue: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis with fixed painful wheals
E.fit: Not here: wheals are transient and pruritic; acute bronchospasm and hypotension present
E.tempting: manifests with urticarial skin lesions

nodes.text: Acute onset urticaria + bronchospasm or hypotension following allergen: diagnose anaphylaxis
Administer intramuscular epinephrine into the anterolateral mid-thigh immediately
Administer high-flow supplemental oxygen and rapid IV crystalloid boluses
**Refractory hypotension or shock:** initiate continuous IV epinephrine infusion
**Persistent bronchospasm:** administer inhaled albuterol
Administer adjunctive IV H1/H2 antihistamines and corticosteroids
Observe for biphasic reactions for minimum 4 to 8 hours

triggers.text: cellulitis of his right leg, and cephalexin therapy was begun

raised, 1 x 2-cm pruritic lesions on the upper and lower extremities and trunk

n-12-n12b1-q040.boardCall: Acute bloody diarrhea + severe cramps without fever or antibiotics -> Escherichia coli O157:H7
n-12-n12b1-q040.hinge: Enterohemorrhagic E. coli O157:H7 produces Shiga toxin causing severe hemorrhagic colitis and bloody diarrhea.
n-12-n12b1-q040.trap: C. difficile requires antibiotic exposure; ETEC causes watery traveler's diarrhea without bright red blood.

A.clue: Pseudomembranous colitis following antibiotic exposure
A.fit: Not here: no recent antibiotic exposure, causes watery rather than grossly bloody diarrhea
A.tempting: common cause of severe colitis and cramping

B.clue: Foodborne watery enterotoxin poisoning or gas gangrene
B.fit: Not here: causes brief non-bloody watery diarrhea, not hemorrhagic colitis
B.tempting: causes acute cramping and foodborne diarrhea

C.clue: Acid-fast protozoan causing chronic watery diarrhea
C.fit: Not here: causes chronic watery diarrhea in immunocompromised, not acute hematochezia
C.tempting: waterborne parasite causing severe abdominal cramps

D.clue: Enterotoxin-mediated secretory traveler diarrhea
D.fit: Not here: produces heat-labile/stable enterotoxins causing watery, non-bloody stool
D.tempting: E. coli strain causing diarrhea after travel

E.clue: Shiga toxin producer causing hemorrhagic colitis
E.fit: Here: bright red blood in stool, severe abdominal cramps, leukocytosis

algorithm.title: Shiga toxin-producing E. coli hemorrhagic colitis

nodes.text: Acute bloody diarrhea + severe abdominal cramps: obtain stool culture and Shiga toxin assay
**Shiga toxin positive or E. coli O157:H7 isolated:** confirm STEC colitis
Provide supportive fluid hydration and avoid antimotility agents
Avoid antibiotics because they increase Shiga toxin release and risk of HUS
**Monitor for hemolytic uremic syndrome:** serial CBC, platelets, and renal function
**HUS develops (anemia, thrombocytopenia, AKI):** supportive care + hemodialysis

triggers.text: two bowel movements containing bright red blood during the past 6 hours

takes no medications
diffuse severe tenderness with no peritoneal signs
leukocyte count is 12,300/mm³

n-12-n12b1-q041.boardCall: Schizophrenia patient states intention to stop pills after discharge -> change to long-acting injectable antipsychotic
n-12-n12b1-q041.hinge: Repeated nonadherence and explicit refusal of post-discharge oral medication warrants long-acting injectable antipsychotics.
n-12-n12b1-q041.trap: Involuntary commitment is for acute danger, but planned nonadherence in stable patient is addressed with long-acting formulations.

A.clue: Prolonging inpatient stay until paranoia clears
A.fit: Not here: does not prevent post-discharge nonadherence once outpatient
A.tempting: ensures patient is fully stable before discharge

B.clue: Depot injection formulation ensuring outpatient medication delivery
B.fit: Here: multiple admissions, states he will stop pills when discharged

C.clue: Involuntary civil commitment without acute danger
C.fit: Not here: not acutely suicidal or homicidal; involuntary commitment unjustified
C.tempting: patient lacks insight and refuses outpatient medication

D.clue: Routine outpatient referral without adherence support
D.fit: Not here: passive referral guarantees rapid medication discontinuation and relapse
D.tempting: respects patient autonomy after inpatient discharge

E.clue: Dose escalation to force disease insight
E.fit: Not here: higher doses cause severe adverse effects without instilling insight
E.tempting: higher doses might overcome paranoid lack of insight

nodes.text: Schizophrenia exacerbation with recurrent relapse: assess medication adherence history
Switch oral antipsychotic to long-acting injectable formulation to ensure adherence
**First-line LAI options:** administer monthly paliperidone, aripiprazole, or haloperidol
Ensure tolerability of oral formulation prior to administering initial injectable dose
**Severe treatment resistance (failed >= 2 antipsychotics):** trial oral clozapine
Coordinate assertive community treatment and outpatient case management

n-12-n12b1-q042.boardCall: 3-mm distal ureteral stone + normal renal function -> oral hydration and analgesia
n-12-n12b1-q042.hinge: Ureteral calculi < 5 mm in stable pediatric patients pass spontaneously with oral hydration and pain control.
n-12-n12b1-q042.trap: Lithotripsy is reserved for large stones (> 10 mm) or failure to pass; 3-mm stone needs hydration.

A.clue: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor for uric acid stones
A.fit: Not here: radiopaque stone is likely calcium oxalate; allopurinol is long-term prevention
A.tempting: prevents uric acid nephrolithiasis formation

B.clue: Conservative fluid therapy promoting spontaneous stone expulsion
B.fit: Here: 3-mm pelvic stone, normal renal function, stable child with colic

C.clue: Thiazide diuretic reducing urinary calcium excretion
C.fit: Not here: prophylactic agent for recurrent stones, not acute 3-mm stone management
C.tempting: reduces urinary calcium excretion long term

D.clue: Urinary alkalinizer dissolving uric acid stones
D.fit: Not here: urine pH 6.5, radiopaque stone indicates calcium, not uric acid
D.tempting: alkalinizes urine to treat nephrolithiasis

E.clue: Vitamin B6 reducing primary hyperoxaluria excretion
E.fit: Not here: ineffective for acute stone passage in uncomplicated nephrolithiasis
E.tempting: proposed therapy for calcium oxalate stone prevention

F.clue: Extracorporeal shock-wave fragmentation of large calculi
F.fit: Not here: stones < 5 mm pass spontaneously without invasive procedural fragmentation
F.tempting: indicated for non-passing calculi larger than 6 mm

nodes.text: Colicky flank pain + hematuria + radiopaque pelvic stone: assess stone size and stability
**Uncomplicated stone < 5 mm:** prescribe oral hydration + analgesics for spontaneous passage
**Stone 5 to 10 mm:** trial medical expulsive therapy with alpha-1 blocker
**Urosepsis, intractable pain, or stone > 10 mm:** urgent urologic stenting or lithotripsy
Strain urine to capture calculus for crystallographic analysis
Perform 24-hour urine metabolic evaluation to guide recurrence prevention

n-12-n12b1-q043.boardCall: Ptosis + abducens weakness + anterior mediastinal mass -> repetitive nerve stimulation test
n-12-n12b1-q043.hinge: Fatigable ocular weakness with a mediastinal thymoma indicates myasthenia gravis, confirmed by repetitive stimulation studies.
n-12-n12b1-q043.trap: Spine MRI and nerve biopsy evaluate radiculopathy or neuropathy, but neuromuscular junction failure requires repetitive stimulation.

A.clue: Electrophysiologic decrement testing neuromuscular junction fatigue
A.fit: Here: ptosis, abducens palsy, generalized fatigable weakness, anterior mediastinal mass

B.clue: Spinal cord neuroimaging for cervical myelopathy
B.fit: Not here: ptosis and cranial nerve abducens weakness cannot originate in cervical cord
B.tempting: evaluates progressive upper and lower extremity weakness

C.clue: Sensory tract evoked potential monitoring
C.fit: Not here: myasthenia is pure motor neuromuscular junction dysfunction without sensory deficit
C.tempting: tests central nervous system sensory conduction pathways

D.clue: Invasive nerve histology for vasculitic neuropathy
D.fit: Not here: cranial nerve weakness and normal reflexes point to neuromuscular junction
D.tempting: evaluates severe peripheral neuropathies or mononeuritis multiplex

E.clue: Muscle histology for inflammatory myopathies
E.fit: Not here: polymyositis causes proximal limb weakness without cranial nerve ptosis
E.tempting: investigates generalized muscle weakness and fatigue

nodes.text: Fatigable ocular or bulbar muscle weakness + anterior mediastinal mass: evaluate for myasthenia gravis
Perform repetitive nerve stimulation studies or single-fiber electromyography
**Decremental muscle action potential response:** confirms neuromuscular transmission defect
Check serum anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies and anti-MuSK antibodies
Obtain chest CT with contrast to fully characterize thymoma
**Treatment initiation:** prescribe oral pyridostigmine + consult surgery for thymectomy

n-12-n12b1-q044.boardCall: Lactating woman + smooth mobile cystic breast lump without fever -> fine-needle aspiration of mass
n-12-n12b1-q044.hinge: A galactocele is a retention cyst of breast milk; fine-needle aspiration yields milky fluid for diagnosis and cure.
n-12-n12b1-q044.trap: Mastitis or abscess presents with erythema, calor, and fever; afebrile cystic mass is a galactocele.

A.clue: Dopamine agonist suppressing pituitary prolactin secretion
A.fit: Not here: normal lactation physiology, cystic mass requires diagnostic decompression
A.tempting: suppresses lactation to treat breast mass

B.clue: Penicillinase-resistant penicillin for bacterial mastitis
B.fit: Not here: afebrile without breast erythema, warmth, or purulent drainage
B.tempting: common treatment for postpartum breast inflammation

C.clue: Premature cessation of normal maternal lactation
C.fit: Not here: weaning does not resolve retention cyst and harms infant nutrition
C.tempting: stopping breastfeeding may reduce milk retention cyst

D.clue: Needle decompression obtaining diagnostic milky fluid
D.fit: Here: lactating woman, 3-cm smooth mobile cystic tender mass, afebrile

E.clue: Altering nursing frequency on affected breast
E.fit: Not here: nursing changes alone do not reliably decompress obstructed galactocele
E.tempting: encourages ductal emptying through increased infant suction

nodes.text: Palpable cystic breast mass in lactating woman without erythema or fever: suspect galactocele
Perform diagnostic and therapeutic fine-needle aspiration yielding milky fluid
**Complete collapse after aspiration:** confirm diagnosis and provide reassurance
**Signs of infection (fever, purulence):** treat as breast abscess with drainage + antibiotics
Encourage continued uninterrupted breastfeeding from both breasts
**Recurrent symptomatic cyst:** repeat aspiration or elective surgical excision

n-12-n12b1-q045.boardCall: Asymptomatic 18-year-old with normal ECG and benign murmur -> no management indicated
n-12-n12b1-q045.hinge: Innocent physiologic systolic ejection murmur with normal ECG and no family history of sudden death requires reassurance only.
n-12-n12b1-q045.trap: Light-headedness while playing basketball tempts sports restriction, but normal ECG and fixed benign murmur exclude HCM.

A.clue: Surgical valvuloplasty for congenital aortic valve stenosis
A.fit: Not here: soft murmur without ejection click, normal ECG, no valve disease
A.tempting: indicated if murmur represents congenital bicuspid aortic stenosis

B.clue: Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator for lethal arrhythmias
B.fit: Not here: normal ECG, no channelopathy, no history of ventricular arrhythmias
B.tempting: prevents sudden death in young athletes

C.clue: Athletic disqualification for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
C.fit: Not here: murmur does not increase with Valsalva; ECG is normal
C.tempting: light-headedness while playing basketball suggests hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

D.clue: Oral anticoagulation for cardiac thromboembolism
D.fit: Not here: no fixed splitting of S2, normal sinus rhythm, no intracardiac shunt
D.tempting: prevents paradoxical embolization in congenital heart defects

E.clue: Reassurance for benign physiologic innocent heart murmur
E.fit: Here: healthy 18-year-old, normal ECG, murmur unchanged with Valsalva

algorithm.title: Evaluation of innocent versus pathologic cardiac murmurs

nodes.text: Systolic murmur in young athlete: evaluate for pathologic cardiac disease features
Perform 12-lead ECG to rule out pre-excitation, prolonged QT, or ventricular hypertrophy
**Pathologic features (diastolic, holosystolic, Valsalva increase):** obtain echocardiogram
Confirm benign innocent flow murmur when ECG and cardiac history are normal
Reassure patient and allow unrestricted competitive athletic participation
**New symptoms (exertional syncope, chest pain):** reassess with cardiology referral

murmur does not change with inspiration, position, or Valsalva maneuver
An ECG shows no abnormalities

n-12-n12b1-q046.boardCall: Syncope + hypoxia + respiratory alkalosis with elevated A-a gradient on OCP -> pulmonary embolism
n-12-n12b1-q046.hinge: Acute syncope, tachycardia, hypoxemia (PaO2 62), and acute respiratory alkalosis on oral contraceptives signify PE.
n-12-n12b1-q046.trap: Panic episode causes respiratory alkalosis and diaphoresis, but PaO2 is normal, unlike this hypoxemic patient.

A.clue: Bronchospasm with expiratory wheezing and air trapping
A.fit: Not here: examination shows clear lungs without wheezing, syncope is atypical
A.tempting: patient has past history of asthma

B.clue: Elevated filling pressures with pulmonary crackles and S3
B.fit: Not here: afebrile, lungs clear, no peripheral edema or jugular distension
B.tempting: causes acute shortness of breath and hypoxemia

C.clue: Hyperventilation alkalosis with normal oxygenation
C.fit: Not here: severe hypoxemia (PaO2 62 mm Hg) with widened A-a gradient
C.tempting: known panic disorder, sudden diaphoresis in crowded mall

D.clue: Focal alveolar consolidation with fever and purulent sputum
D.fit: Not here: afebrile, normal leukocyte count, acute syncope presentation
D.tempting: causes acute hypoxemia and tachypnea

E.clue: V/Q mismatch with hypoxemic respiratory alkalosis and syncope
E.fit: Here: syncope, oral contraceptive use, tachycardia, PaO2 62, PaCO2 30

algorithm.title: Acute pulmonary embolism diagnosis and risk stratification

nodes.text: Acute syncope + hypoxemia + tachycardia in patient on estrogen: evaluate for pulmonary embolism
Calculate Wells score and obtain CT pulmonary angiography immediately
**Hemodynamic instability (systolic BP < 90 mm Hg):** bedside echocardiogram + systemic thrombolysis
**Hemodynamically stable with confirmed PE:** initiate therapeutic anticoagulation
Assess right ventricular strain with troponin, BNP, and echocardiogram
**Contraindication to anticoagulation:** place inferior vena cava filter

n-12-n12b1-q047.boardCall: Back pain + anemia + hypercalcemia + renal failure + rouleaux -> bone marrow biopsy
n-12-n12b1-q047.hinge: CRAB features (hypercalcemia, renal dysfunction, anemia, bone pain) with rouleaux formation require bone marrow biopsy to confirm myeloma.
n-12-n12b1-q047.trap: Macrocytic anemia tempts B12 testing, but hypercalcemia, azotemia, and rouleaux indicate multiple myeloma.

A.clue: Hepatic biochemical profile for hepatocellular injury
A.fit: Not here: nonspecific test that cannot confirm plasma cell marrow neoplasm
A.tempting: screens for systemic organ involvement

B.clue: Evaluation for pernicious anemia or malabsorption
B.fit: Not here: macrocytosis secondary to rouleaux aggregation, hypercalcemia, and renal azotemia
B.tempting: evaluates macrocytic anemia with MCV 103

C.clue: Iron and ferritin studies for microcytic anemia
C.fit: Not here: MCV is elevated (103 µm³); hypercalcemia and azotemia signify myeloma
C.tempting: common workup for newly discovered anemia

D.clue: Lower gastrointestinal endoscopy evaluating occult bleeding
D.fit: Not here: bone pain, hypercalcemia, and rouleaux point to hematologic malignancy
D.tempting: investigates occult gastrointestinal blood loss anemia

E.clue: Histologic confirmation of clonal plasma cell marrow infiltration
E.fit: Here: low back pain, anemia, calcium 10.9 mg/dL, creatinine 1.8, rouleaux

algorithm.title: Multiple myeloma diagnostic confirmation and management

nodes.text: CRAB features (hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia, bone pain) + rouleaux: suspect plasma cell myeloma
Perform bone marrow aspiration and biopsy with flow cytometry to confirm diagnosis
**Clonal bone marrow plasma cells >= 10%:** confirms multiple myeloma
Obtain serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation, and serum free light chains
Perform whole-body low-dose CT or skeletal survey for osteolytic bone lesions
**Symptomatic myeloma:** initiate induction chemotherapy (bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone)

algorithm.title: Adult immunization in men who have sex with men

nodes.text: Routine health maintenance in sexually active MSM: evaluate immunization status and STI risks
Administer 2-dose hepatitis A vaccine series for high-risk exposure protection
Confirm completion of hepatitis B vaccination series or check surface antibody titer
Administer HPV vaccine series through age 26 (or through 45 with shared decision-making)
Screen for HIV, syphilis, gonorrhea, and chlamydia at all anatomic exposure sites
**HIV-negative with condomless sex:** prescribe HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis

n-12-n12b1-q049.trap: Combat nightmares tempt PTSD, but paroxysmal 10-minute choking spells with panic attacks out of the blue are panic disorder.

B.tempting: non-addictive anxiolytic medication

C.fit: Not here: no psychosis, high risk of extrapyramidal motor side effects
C.tempting: rapid tranquilization for severe acute agitation

nodes.text: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks peaking within 10 minutes + anticipatory anxiety: diagnose panic disorder
Prescribe first-line selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (paroxetine or sertraline)
**Alternative first-line:** trial serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (venlafaxine)
Initiate cognitive behavioral therapy focused on interoceptive exposure
**Acute severe incapacitating panic attacks:** bridge short-term benzodiazepine during SSRI titration
**Treatment-resistant panic disorder:** switch to another SSRI/SNRI or tricyclic antidepressant

nodes.text: Pelvic ring fracture + blood at urethral meatus or perineal hematoma: suspect urethral disruption

n-12-q080.trap: Sudden dyspnea tempts heparin for PE, but pulmonary crackles, S3, and new murmurs indicate acute valve failure.

algorithm.title: Acute valvular destruction in infective endocarditis

nodes.text: Infective endocarditis patient developing acute pulmonary edema + new murmurs: suspect valve rupture
Perform emergent transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography
**Severe acute regurgitation with heart failure:** consult cardiac surgery for urgent replacement
Administer intravenous vasodilators and diuretics for pulmonary congestion if stable
**Cardiogenic shock present:** initiate inotropes and avoid balloon pump in aortic regurgitation
Continue targeted bactericidal intravenous antibiotic therapy

n-12-q082.hinge: Fleeting pulmonary infiltrates, recurrent mucous plugs, and central bronchiectasis define ABPA.

nodes.text: Recognize poorly controlled asthma or CF + recurrent brown mucous plugs
Screening labs: peripheral eosinophilia + serum total IgE > 1000 IU/mL
Diagnostic testing: Aspergillus skin test reactivity + serum Aspergillus-specific IgE/IgG
Chest CT: central bronchiectasis + mucoid impaction with branching opacities
Acute flare treatment: oral prednisone taper
**Recurrent flares or steroid-sparing needed:** add oral itraconazole
**Refractory severe disease:** consider monoclonal anti-IgE (omalizumab)

n-12-q083.trap: Vaccination was completed, tempting belief that immunization alone is sufficient protection.

nodes.text: Recognize loss of splenic opsonization and clearance of encapsulated bacteria
Administer 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate + 23-valent polysaccharide vaccines

Daily oral penicillin prophylaxis until at least age 5 and for 1-2 years postsplenectomy

Provide emergency supply of amoxicillin-clavulanate for acute fever at home
**Febrile illness occurs:** urgent blood cultures + immediate IV ceftriaxone

n-12-q084.hinge: Pancreatic insufficiency and low BMI (16) require aggressive caloric supplementation to support fetal growth.
n-12-q084.trap: Cystic fibrosis pulmonary concerns distract from the baseline extreme malnutrition and pregnancy caloric demands.

A.clue: Antimicrobial treatment indicated for acute pulmonary exacerbations

algorithm.title: Preconception and pregnancy care in cystic fibrosis

nodes.text: Review preconception pulmonary function (FEV1) and baseline nutrition
Optimize nutritional status prior to and throughout pregnancy
**BMI < 22 kg/m2 or suboptimal weight gain:** high-calorie diet + enteral feeds + pancreatic enzymes
Screen for cystic fibrosis-related diabetes with 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test
**Elevated fasting or postprandial glucose:** start subcutaneous insulin
Continue chest physiotherapy + inhaled mucolytics + inhaled bronchodilators
**Acute pulmonary exacerbation:** targeted antipseudomonal IV antibiotics
Screen partner for CFTR mutations to assess fetal cystic fibrosis risk

n-12-q085.boardCall: Infant with acute bacterial meningitis -> Sensorineural hearing loss
n-12-q085.hinge: Sensorineural hearing loss is the single most common long-term sequela of acute bacterial meningitis.
n-12-q085.trap: Subdural effusions occur frequently in infants with H influenzae, but usually resolve spontaneously.

A.clue: Focal spinal or intracranial collection from direct extension
A.fit: Not here: localized suppurative collection rather than generalized meningeal sequela
A.tempting: bacterial spreading can cause localized parameningeal pus collections

B.clue: Suppurative cochlear inflammation causing permanent auditory deficit
B.fit: Here: acute bacterial meningitis carries highest long-term risk of sensorineural hearing loss

C.clue: Aqueductal obstruction by purulent exudate causing ventriculomegaly
C.fit: Not here: obstructive hydrocephalus occurs far less frequently than auditory impairment
C.tempting: thick meningeal exudate can obstruct ventricular outflow pathways

D.clue: Persistent unprovoked seizures secondary to cortical necrosis
D.fit: Not here: secondary epilepsy occurs less frequently than post-infectious hearing deficit
D.tempting: acute seizures are common during acute meningeal inflammation

E.clue: Reactive sterile subdural fluid collection in young infants
E.fit: Not here: common transient finding that typically resolves spontaneously without deficits
E.tempting: common transient finding on neuroimaging in infant meningitis

algorithm.title: Acute bacterial meningitis in infants: complications and management

nodes.text: Recognize acute purulent meningitis: fever + bulging fontanel + CSF pleocytosis
Most common long-term complication is sensorineural hearing loss from cochlear inflammation
Immediate treatment: empiric IV vancomycin + ceftriaxone + dexamethasone
**Infant < 1 month:** add IV ampicillin for Listeria monocytogenes
Perform formal audiology screening prior to hospital discharge
**Severe hearing deficit:** timely referral for cochlear implantation
Monitor serial head circumferences to detect communicative hydrocephalus

nodes.text: Confirm primary amenorrhea: age > 15 with secondary sexual traits, or > 13 without
Pelvic ultrasound: assess presence of uterus and ovaries
**Uterus present:** check serum FSH and LH concentrations
**FSH elevated (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism):** order karyotype analysis
**FSH low or normal:** brain MRI to evaluate hypothalamic-pituitary lesions
**Uterus absent:** order karyotype + serum testosterone (Müllerian agenesis vs androgen insensitivity)
**Turner syndrome (45,X):** echocardiogram + renal ultrasound + hormone replacement

nodes.text: Recognize herald patch: solitary oval 2-5 cm salmon-colored plaque on chest or trunk
Secondary eruption: symmetric oval plaques along skin cleavage lines (Christmas-tree pattern)
Examine differential: secondary syphilis (palms/soles involved), tinea corporis, guttate psoriasis
**Sexually active or palm/sole lesions:** check rapid plasma reagin (RPR)
Reassure patient: self-resolving exanthem within 6-8 weeks
**Mild pruritus:** topical emollients or low-potency topical corticosteroids
**Severe pruritus:** oral antihistamines or brief phototherapy

n-12-q088.trap: Infantile constipation tempts rectal biopsy for Hirschsprung, but macroglossia points to hypothyroidism.

A.fit: Not here: does not explain macroglossia, open posterior fontanel, or gross delay

Check newborn screening status (often missed in home births)
Diagnostic confirmation: serum TSH + free thyroxine (free T4)
**Elevated TSH + low free T4:** primary congenital hypothyroidism
Initiate prompt oral levothyroxine to prevent permanent cognitive impairment
Monitor free T4 and TSH every 1-2 months during infancy
**Persistent TSH elevation:** increase levothyroxine dose

algorithm.title: Immunization schedule in adults with HIV

nodes.text: Review immunization history and CD4 count in HIV
Pneumococcal vaccination: give PCV followed by PPSV23 series
**5 years after initial PPSV23 dose:** administer repeat PPSV23 vaccination
Hepatitis B series: test anti-HBs; revaccinate if titers inadequate
Annual influenza vaccination + COVID-19 booster
Administer recombinant zoster vaccine to all patients age > 50 (or > 19 with immunosuppression)
Avoid live vaccines (MMR, varicella) if CD4 count < 200/mm3

n-12-q090.boardCall: Short bowel syndrome on prolonged TPN + direct hyperbilirubinemia -> Cholestatic hepatic disease

nodes.text: Recognize risk: short bowel syndrome + prolonged TPN (> 2-4 weeks) + lack of enteral intake
Laboratory profile: predominant direct hyperbilirubinemia + mild alkaline phosphatase rise + normal transaminases
Right upper quadrant ultrasound: exclude biliary sludge, cholelithiasis, or ductal dilatation
Promote enteral feeding: even minimal trophic enteral nutrition stimulates gallbladder motility
Optimize TPN: reduce excessive dextrose and replace standard soy lipids with fish-oil emulsions
**Progressive cholestasis despite enteral feeds:** add ursodeoxycholic acid
Monitor for end-stage liver disease and consideration of intestinal transplantation
